questions.question: Which event is closest to an elastic collision?
questions.explanation: Billiard balls bounce apart with little deformation.

questions.question: In an inelastic collision, kinetic energy may become
questions.explanation: Some kinetic energy changes into other forms.

questions.question: Objects often stick together or deform in an inelastic collision.
questions.explanation: Sticking and deformation are common in inelastic collisions.

questions.question: Momentum is never considered in collision analysis.
questions.explanation: Momentum is central to collision analysis.

questions.question: A collision where objects bounce apart and kinetic energy is mostly conserved is ________.
questions.explanation: Elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy approximately.

questions.question: How can a model show the difference between elastic and inelastic collisions?
questions.correctAnswer: A good answer compares bouncing apart with sticking/deforming.
questions.explanation: A model can use balls that bounce for elastic collisions and clay that sticks for inelastic collisions.
